what_its_for: Tranexamic acid helps stop or reduce heavy bleeding. It is most commonly used to treat heavy menstrual periods (heavy monthly bleeding) in women. It may also be used before or after surgery, dental procedures, or to treat other types of bleeding problems. It works by helping your blood clot more effectively and preventing clots from breaking down too soon.
how_to_take: Take tranexamic acid exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets. If you are taking it for heavy periods, start taking it on the first day of your period when bleeding begins. Do not take it more days than prescribed.
dosing: For heavy menstrual bleeding, the usual dose is 1,300 mg (two 650 mg tablets) taken 3 times a day for up to 5 days during your period. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have kidney problems. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different depending on why you are taking this medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store tranexamic acid at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking hormonal birth control (such as the pill, patch, or ring) at the same time without talking to your doctor first, as this combination may increase your risk of blood clots. Avoid this medicine if you have ever had a blood clot in your legs, lungs, or brain, or if you have color vision problems. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially blood thinners or clot-preventing medicines. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery if you feel dizzy.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden chest pain or difficulty breathing, coughing up blood, sudden leg pain or swelling, sudden severe headache or vision changes, numbness or weakness on one side of your body, slurred speech, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face and throat. Also call your doctor if your heavy bleeding does not improve, or if you notice any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Tranexamic acid starts working within a few hours of taking it. Most women notice a significant reduction in their heavy menstrual bleeding within the first 1 to 2 days of starting treatment. It only works while you are actively taking it during your period and does not build up in your system between cycles.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor may lower your dose if your kidneys do not work well, since this medicine is removed from the body through the kidneys. Older adults: Use with caution; your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of this medicine may pass into breast milk; discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Safety and dosing for children have not been fully established for heavy menstrual bleeding; follow your doctor's specific guidance.
